page.layout: One printed page (left page of the opening). Running text in one main column, centred on the page; a narrow column of marginal notes at the right edge, cut off by the gutter. Below the text: no further blocks. Reading order: running head and page number at top, then the main column top to bottom, then the right-margin notes.

main_text.p: tillantes oculos: molli quadam teneritudine, cordis fauciante meditulliū: Totus deditítius, totus impensus, diffluit inter deperiendū, & perit. Adeò præcipitat hic semita, malè cauti Puberes, quæ de FiGto vergit in Serium: Et ut alibi sit latum satis, Genuinum inter & Simulata discrimen; certè mimesis amoris, amor est.
main_text.head: Quæstio XXIII.
An, quod illustres quidam Auctores fecerunt, commentitias Historias edere conveniat.
main_text.p: Soror historiæ, fabula: Magis arctum est inter illas, quàm imperiti putent contubernium: Fidelissimus etiam Commentator multum habet de Poëta: Extemporales inter gesta

page.notes: The right-hand marginal notes are cut off by the gutter and only partly legible (fragments such as "Quest.", "quæ vulgo", "mixta", "commu", "quoque", "dclcunt", "memor", "firinge", "circum"); they are not transcribed. The first word of the question paragraph is a large woodcut initial "S", read as "Soror" with the initial joined. The first line "Soror" may read "Oror" in the scan; the initial letter is the large S and is given as printed in the heading block. Head levels for the question title are approximate.
